title: The Conversion Markup Applied to an Air Ticket Fare Brands Service Charge
content:
Where the fare lines of an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking were presented in a currency other than US dollars, a conversion markup is applied last to the sum settled as the agency service charge. Which markup applies turns on where the contracting company on the Corporate Travel Programmes side is registered.

## 1. The markup

1.1 Where the booking's fare lines were presented in a currency other than US dollars and the contracting company is registered outside the United States, the fare brand's own conversion markup is applied, as scheduled for the Air Ticket Fare Brands brand the booking is held in.

1.2 Where the booking's fare lines were presented in a currency other than US dollars and the contracting company is registered in the United States, the domestic conversion markup of 1.0 percent is applied.

1.3 In every other case no such markup is applied.

## 2. What is read, and from where

The currency read is the one recorded on the most recent base-fare line standing on the booking. The country of registration is the country recorded for the contracting company on the Corporate Travel Programmes programme standing against the booking.

Both of the first two rows open on the fare lines having been presented in a currency other than US dollars; a booking whose fare lines were presented in US dollars falls to the last row whatever the company's country.

## 3. Truth table

| Currency of the fare lines | The contracting company is registered | Markup applied |
| --- | --- | --- |
| other than US dollars | outside the United States | the fare brand's own conversion markup |
| other than US dollars | in the United States | 1.0 percent |
| US dollars | either | no such markup |

## 4. Hypothetical readings

A booking whose most recent base-fare line was presented in euros, against a company registered in Ireland: the fare brand's own conversion markup is applied.

The same booking against a company registered in the United States: 1.0 percent is applied, whatever markup the brand itself carries.

A booking whose most recent base-fare line was presented in US dollars, against a company registered in Ireland: no such markup is applied.
